div.head: I Cn 24
div.ab: And we lærað, þæt man wið fúlne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthæmed ⁊ wið æghwylcne æwbryce warnige symle.
⁊ we lærað, þæt man wiþ fulne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthǽmed ⁊ wið æghwylce ǽwbryce warnian georne.
And we lærað, þæt man wið fulne galscype ⁊ wið unrihthæmed ⁊ wið æghwylcne æwbrece wærnige symle.
Et ab inmundis gaudiis (a libidine) et iniusto concubitu uel adulterio caueatur.
Docemus quoque, ut ab incesta lasciuia et iniusta uenere, necnon et qualibet legis transgressione prudenter sibi caueat.
⁊ we lærað þæt man wið fulne galscipe ⁊ wið unrihthǽmed ⁊ wið æghwylce ǽwbryce warnian georne.
And we lærað þæt man wið fulne galscipe and wið unrihthæmed and wið æghwylcne æwbryce warnige symle.
Und wir schreiben vor, dass man vor schmutziger Geilheit und vor gesetzwidrigem Beischlaf und vor jedem Ehebruch sich stets (ernstlich B) hüte.
And we instruct that people always (eagerly, B) beware of foul lust and unlawful intercourse and every kind of adultery.
And we enjoin that foul lasciviousness and illicit unions and every [kind of] adultery be zealously abhorred.
And we instruct that foul lust, illicit intercourse, and all forms of adultery are to be zealously avoided.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 305, October 2026 (MS Cons)

a l. above i. g. Dm; id est a l. in the text T; lacking in the others
Hieraus Hom. n. Wulfstan 308. Unkanon. Ehe mitgemeint
From this Hom. n. Wulfstan 308. Uncanonical marriage is also meant
Gegen Unzucht (s. d. Gl 4a) auch I 6, 3. 7, 2. II 55
Against unchastity (see that word in Gl 4a) also I 6, 3. 7, 2. II 55
Das Wort veraltet (obwohl eubruche noch Mittelengl. ‘Ehebruch’); daher der Fehler in Cons = II 6. 50, der umgekehrte wie o. S. 68¹⁵
The word became obsolete (although eubruche still means ‘adultery’ in Middle English); hence the error in Cons = II 6. 50, the reverse of that above p. 68¹⁵
Cf. V Atr. 25; VI, 28, 2; Procl. of 1020, cap. 15; II Cn. 6; Wulfstan, p. 298. Cons. misunderstands the word ǽwbryce and translates it qualibet legis transgressione both here and in II, 6.
